BMI_Clinical_Note: BMI 25–29.9 — Indian Obese Class I. Significant metabolic & BC recurrence risk. Mediterranean diet + exercise.
Waist_Risk_Indian: Central Obesity (≥80 cm — Indian Women Threshold)
Bone_Density_Concern: LOW-MODERATE — Routine monitoring. Adequate dietary calcium (dairy/ragi/sesame) + exercise.
Nutrition_Impact_Symptoms: Diarrhea; Fatigue; Hot Flashes (Hormone Therapy); Menopausal Symptoms; Neutropenia-related (risk); Weight Loss
Vitamin_D_IU_per_day: 400 IU/day (ICMR-NIN 2020 RDA) — sunlight 15–20 min/day also essential
Calcium_mg_per_day: 600 mg/day (ICMR-NIN 2020 RDA) — dietary calcium from dairy/ragi/sesame preferred
Zinc_mg_per_day: 10 mg/day (ICMR-NIN 2020) — important for immune function + wound healing
Dietary_Fibre_g_per_day: 40 g/day (ICMR-NIN 2020); reduce to 25 g if diarrhoea/mucositis
Omega3_Recommendation: 2–3 g EPA/DHA/day — fish oil supplement [ESPEN B5-7]
Protein_Source_Note: Vegetarian protein: dal+rice combo (complete AA), paneer, curd, soya, moong, rajma, chickpeas, tofu, amaranth
Alcohol_Guidance: ZERO alcohol — carcinogen; increases BC recurrence risk [ESPEN C5-2]
ICMR_NIN_2020_Reference: ICMR-NIN Nutrient Requirements & RDA for Indians (2020 revision)
Nutrition_Route_ESPEN: ONS (Pentasure/Ensure/Fresubin) → EN if oral <50% target >1 week → PN if EN not feasible [ESPEN B3-3]
Supplement_Recommendation: ONS 1–2x/day: Pentasure HP / Ensure Plus / Fresubin Energy / Disprolene (Indian brands preferred); Calcium 600 mg/day (ICMR-NIN 2020 RDA) + Vitamin D 400 IU/day + 15–20 min daily sunlight; Vitamin B12 1–2 mcg/day (ICMR-NIN 2020) or 500 mcg/week cyanocobalamin — B12 deficiency common in Indian vegetarians; Algae-based DHA 200–500 mg/day (omega-3 for vegetarian Indian BC patients); Iron 19–29 mg/day (ICMR-NIN 2020) — monitor Hb; IV iron if <8 g/dL on chemo; Folate 220–400 mcg/day (ICMR-NIN 2020; higher during chemo); Ground flaxseed 1–2 tbsp/day (lignans — phytoestrogen modulation; beneficial ER+ Indian BC survivors); Multivitamin/mineral at RDA dose ONLY (ICMR-NIN 2020). NOT high-dose. Avoid selenium, Vit E, Vit C megadoses during chemo.
Exercise_Plan_ESPEN_India: Aerobic: Brisk walk 45 min/day OR 150–300 min/week (cycling, swimming, Zumba, yoga) [ESPEN B4-1/C5-1]; Resistance: 2–3x/week, 8–12 reps, major muscle groups; can use resistance bands/body weight at home [ESPEN B4-2]; Yoga: 3–5x/week (Suryanamaskar, Pranayama, Shavasana) — evidence for fatigue reduction + cortisol in Indian BC survivors; TARGET: 150–300 min/week moderate activity — reduces Indian BC recurrence risk and improves overall survival
ESPEN_Guidelines_India: 📋 SCREENING [B1-1]: Regular nutritional assessment from diagnosis. Indian BC patients — ICMR/WHO Asian BMI cut-offs apply (Normal: 18.5–22.9; Overweight: ≥23; Obese: ≥25). [North India (UP/Delhi/Punjab/Haryana)] | 📋 ASSESSMENT [B1-2]: PG-SGA score elevated → quantitative assessment: 24-hr dietary recall, muscle mass (BIA/DEXA/mid-arm circumference), grip strength, CRP/albumin, NIS. | ⚡ ENERGY [B2-1]: 25–30 kcal/kg/day (ESPEN). Indian context: average Indian BC woman body weight 55–65 kg. Total: 1400–2000 kcal/day depending on stage and activity. | 🥩 PROTEIN [B2-2]: >1 g/kg/day (ESPEN); ICMR-NIN 2020 RDA: 0.83 g/kg/day (healthy); BC treatment: 1.0–1.5 g/kg/day. Vegetarian patients: dal+rice+dairy combination essential for complete amino acid profile. | 💊 MICRONUTRIENTS [B2-4 + ICMR-NIN 2020]: Vitamin D (endemic deficiency in India — 400–1000 IU/day), Calcium (600–1200 mg/day from ragi/dairy/sesame), Iron (19–29 mg/day), Folate (220–400 mcg/day). AVOID high-dose antioxidants during chemo. | ⚠ INDIAN OBESITY [Obese Class I]: Indian BMI ≥25 = Obese. Metabolic syndrome highly prevalent. Obesity is independent risk factor for BC recurrence and mortality in Indian women. Weight management essential post-treatment. | 🚨 NUTRITION [B3-1]: IMMEDIATE intervention. ONS (Pentasure/Ensure/Fresubin); escalate to EN if oral <50% target >1 week. | ⚠ INTERVENTION [B3-2]: No unproven restrictive diets. Beware of social media misinformation about 'anti-cancer' diets in Indian context. | 🏥 MEDICAL NUTRITION [B3-3]: EN preferred (nasogastric/PEG); PN if EN not feasible. | ⚠ REFEEDING [B3-4]: Slow reintroduction if prolonged malnutrition. Monitor PO4, K+, Mg2+. Vitamin B1 200–300 mg/day. | 🔴 TNBC [Indian]: High incidence in young premenopausal Indian women. Aggressive chemo → highest nutritional risk. Protein priority 1.5–2.0 g/kg/day. Anti-inflammatory diet. Immunotherapy GI AE management. | 🏋 EXERCISE [B4-1/B4-2]: Aerobic + resistance training recommended. Yoga as adjunct for Indian patients (evidence for fatigue, QoL, cortisol reduction). Lymphedema: progressive resistance IS SAFE. | ❌ BEWARE: High-dose supplement marketing targeting Indian cancer patients (social media/WhatsApp) — vitamin megadoses, 'cancer-curing' supplements, unproven herbal products — not recommended without oncologist approval [ESPEN B2-4].
Diet_Chart_Indian_Meal_Plan: 🌅 Breakfast: Fortified dalia/oats porridge (full-fat milk + 1 egg whisked in / extra milk powder 3 tbsp) + banana + 1 tbsp peanut butter + 250 ml ONS (Ensure/Pentasure/Fresubin) + green tea || 🕙 Mid-Morning: High-calorie Indian shake — full-fat milk + banana + 2 tbsp peanut butter/almond butter + 1 tbsp ground flaxseed + 1 tsp jaggery (~450 kcal) + ONS if appetite poor || 🍽 Lunch: Soft dal-rice (1 cup each) + 1 tsp ghee (for calories) + steamed vegetable + full-fat dahi + 1 tbsp til/sesame for calcium || 🕓 Snack: Banana + moong dal khichdi (plain, no spice) + ORS solution 200ml; AVOID: raw vegetables, high fibre, dairy if intolerant, oily/spicy foods; kairi (raw mango) panna without spice can help electrolytes || 🌙 Dinner: Moong dal khichdi (1.5 cups, soft, with ghee 1 tsp) + boiled/steamed fish / paneer curry (soft) + cooked lauki/tinda + warm haldi doodh || 🌛 Bedtime: Full-fat milk (250ml warm) + 1–2 tbsp almond/peanut butter + pinch turmeric OR 250ml ONS supplement || ✅ HOT FLASHES (Tamoxifen/AI): Avoid chai excess, spicy food triggers; cold nimbu pani, chaas (unsweetened) preferred; soya foods (tofu/soy milk) 1–2 servings/day may mildly reduce flashes; flaxseed 1–2 tbsp/day beneficial. || ✅ INDIAN BC DIET PRINCIPLES [ESPEN C5-2 + ICMR-NIN 2020]: Predominantly plant-based. Whole grains (millet/brown rice/multi-grain), pulses (dal/rajma/chana), vegetables (cruciferous 3x/week), fruits (2–3/day), low-fat dairy, minimal oil (mustard/groundnut/coconut — 3–4 tsp/day). || Regional: Emphasise whole wheat chapati, bajra/jowar roti, dal, seasonal sabzi; reduce heavy ghee, cream, paneer excess; increase green leafy vegetables. || 💰 Low SES: Focus on cost-effective anti-cancer foods — seasonal vegetables, local millets, dals, eggs, sprouts. Government schemes: PM Poshan, NFSA for food access. Minimise food waste. Home-cooked preferred. || ⚠ OBESITY (Obese Class I, Indian cut-off ≥25): Obesity significantly increases BC recurrence risk in Indian women. Post-treatment gradual weight loss (0.5 kg/week max). No energy restriction during active treatment. Mediterranean-Indian hybrid diet: dal-sabzi-millet base + minimal ghee/oil. Walk 45 min/day. || 🌱 VEGETARIAN BC PATIENT: Complete protein strategy — dal+rice/roti at same meal (complementary AA), include rajma/chana/lentils daily, paneer/tofu/soya 1–2x/day, dahi 1–2 cups/day, sprouted legumes. B12 supplement if vegan. Omega-3: flaxseed + walnuts + algae-based DHA supplement. || 🔴 TNBC (Indian): Higher prevalence in young Indian women (<40 yrs). Highest metabolic demand. Protein 1.5–2.0 g/kg/day mandatory during chemo. Anti-inflammatory diet: haldi, adrak, omega-3, berries, green tea. Immunotherapy patients: watch for immune-related colitis — low-residue if GI symptoms. || ❌ STRICTLY AVOID [ALL INDIAN BC PATIENTS]: Alcohol, tobacco (paan/gutka), vanaspati/dalda (trans fats), excess ghee in obese patients, maida/refined flour products, packaged namkeen/biscuits, sugar-sweetened drinks (even fruit juice), raw/undercooked meat/eggs during chemo. || 🐟 OMEGA-3 FOR VEGETARIANS: Ground flaxseed (1–2 tbsp/day) + walnuts (5–7/day) + mustard oil for cooking + algae-based DHA supplement (250–500 mg/day) — essential since no fish intake. || 🏃 YOGA + EXERCISE [ESPEN B4-1/B4-2]: Brisk walk 45 min/day + yoga (reduces cortisol/fatigue, improves QoL in Indian BC survivors) + resistance 2–3x/week. Reduces BC recurrence risk significantly.
